strings.name: Hadley Wickham
strings.summary: Hadley Wickham develops R tools such as ggplot2 and leads Posit’s tidyverse team, advancing data preparation, visualization and data-science education. He combines software design, statistical thinking and textbooks to make analysis easier to learn and reuse. The tidyverse is maintained by teams and a community, and his books have co-authors. He did not invent R.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Distinguishes award years from announcement dates and podcast publication from recording. Education follows university sources; old company names and former adjunct titles are not treated as current roles.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced the R tidyverse ecosystem and visualization tools, broadening access to statistical analysis and data-science education.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied human biology, statistics and computer science at Auckland; earned an Iowa State statistics PhD in 2008.
strings.facts.f2.label: Key tools
strings.facts.f2.value: ggplot2 and the tidyverse ecosystem, developed by multiple programmers, maintainers and community contributors.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Statistical graphics and data tidying
strings.highlights.h1.text: Developed ggplot2 and explained data organization for manipulation, modeling and visualization in Tidy Data.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Open data-science education
strings.highlights.h2.text: Co-authored the second edition of R for Data Science with Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Garrett Grolemund, freely readable online.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Participates in a data-science podcast
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Test Set releases an episode with him, colleagues and Posit CEO Tareef Kawaf discussing AI and data science; this is its publication date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Publishes a history of the tidyverse
strings.timeline.t2.text: The journal publishes his retrospective on the move from individual development to teamwork, community collaboration and maintenance.
strings.timeline.t3.title: 2025 ASA award announced
strings.timeline.t3.text: Posit announces his 2025 Statistical Computing and Graphics Award; this is the announcement date, not the 2025 ceremony date.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Second-edition book announcement
strings.timeline.t4.text: The tidyverse blog announces publication of R for Data Science’s second edition, crediting three authors and community contributions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Receives the COPSS Presidents’ Award
strings.timeline.t5.text: The award recognizes statistical computing and outreach; “Nobel Prize of Statistics” is only an informal nickname.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Publishes Tidy Data
strings.timeline.t6.text: The Journal of Statistical Software publishes his account of data tidying through consistent arrangements of variables, observations and tables.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins RStudio
strings.timeline.t7.text: Becomes Chief Scientist; the company later becomes Posit. His website confirms his current role and team leadership.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earns a statistics PhD
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completes his doctorate at Iowa State under Di Cook and Heike Hofmann.
